target_customer: Homeowners who want camera-based break-in prevention
problem: Home security cameras and doorbells needed new wiring or drilling. Kuna put a Wi-Fi camera, intercom and siren inside an outdoor light fixture that replaces the existing one.
business_model: Hardware sales plus a subscription (Kuna Premium) for video features

founders.name: Sai-Wai Fu
founders.background_notes: From the Kuna About page: led development of an early million-transistor microprocessor at Intel and engineering at C-Cube. Not listed on the YC page, which names only Haomiao Huang.

founders.name: Haomiao Huang
founders.background_notes: Per the Kuna About page, built self-driving cars at Caltech and researched multi-rotor drones at Stanford; later joined Kleiner Perkins as an investor.

technical_complexity.rationale: Custom hardware with camera, intercom, siren and wiring fit inside a light fixture, plus firmware, cloud video and a mobile app, needing manufacturing and certification.

defensibility.rationale: Design and patents were filed, but cameras and doorbells from larger vendors could add similar features; no network effects.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The acquirer and date are not found in sources. Kuna kept selling products and launched an AI vehicle recognition platform in 2017.

market_need_then: The October 2014 Indiegogo campaign raised about 229 thousand dollars from about 1,530 backers against a 50 thousand dollar goal, showing early consumer demand.

branding.domain_note: Uses getkuna.com (prefix variant); a separate kunasystems.com also appears.

identity.visual_style: Fixtures offered in craftsman, traditional and contemporary styles in black or bronze per Designboom.
identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as a digital doorman focused on prevention.

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Fox News, TechHive, Designboom and Brit + Co around the 2014 and 2015 launch.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct short name and broad consumer tech press, but no evidence of community or merch.

outcome_analysis: Kuna joined YC in winter 2014, then raised about 229 thousand dollars on Indiegogo in October 2014 and shipped its smart light fixture in 2015. YC lists it as acquired but the buyer, date and price are not public in sources found, and the company website still sells products with no ownership notice, so the outcome cannot be explained further.
notes: No dated competitor source found; the articles opened did not name competitors. The Indiegogo figure and backer count come from search results and a press release, the Indiegogo page was not opened. Seedtable lists a 2014-10 seed with Y Combinator, unverified and not recorded. A 2025 Series A for KUN is a different company. Founded year 2012 is from the company About page.
